title: InputNumber
lead: InputNumber is an input component to provide numerical input.

examples.name: Numerals
prose: InputNumber is used as a controlled input with value and onValueChange properties.

examples.name: Locale
prose: Localization information such as grouping and decimal symbols are defined with the locale property which defaults to the user locale.

examples.name: Currency
prose: Monetary values are enabled by setting mode property as currency. In this setting, currency property also needs to be defined using ISO 4217 standard such as "USD" for the US dollar.

examples.name: Prefix & Suffix
prose: Custom texts e.g. units can be placed before or after the input section with the prefix and suffix properties.

examples.name: Buttons
prose: Spinner buttons are enabled using the showButtons property and layout is defined with the buttonLayout.

examples.name: Vertical
prose: Buttons can also placed vertically by setting buttonLayout as vertical.

examples.name: Float Label
prose: A floating label appears on top of the input field when focused. Visit FloatLabel documentation for more information.

examples.name: Filled
prose: Specify the variant property as filled to display the component with a higher visual emphasis than the default outlined style.

examples.name: Invalid
prose: Invalid state is displayed using the invalid prop to indicate a failed validation. You can use this style when integrating with form validation libraries.

examples.name: Disabled
prose: When disabled is present, the element cannot be edited and focused.

The currency to use in currency formatting. Possible values are the [ISO 4217 currency codes](https://www.six-group.com/en/products-services/financial-information/data-standards.html#scrollTo=maintenance-agency), such as "USD" for the US dollar, "EUR" for the euro, or "CNY" for the Chinese RMB.
There is no default value; if the style is "currency", the currency property must be provided.
